turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come in out of that rain, you look perished. This is Oisín, is it?
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It is, yeah. I'm his mam. He's five and he's not himself.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Oisín, can you tell me what feels wrong?
[SEG0004] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0005] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's after getting a fever and a rash. A boy in the class has measles, so the school texted us.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mm. When did the fever start?
[SEG0007] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thursday night. He went to bed grand and woke up boiling. I've been giving him 5 ml of calpol from the chemist, about every six hours.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the rash itself?
[SEG0009] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yesterday morning on his belly, and now it's on his face and his arms. Off his food too. We missed the cousin's party, bouncy castle and all.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any cough?
[SEG0011] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Not really.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Runny nose, or sore eyes in the light?
[SEG0013] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Never the sore eyes. His nose is grand.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any long-term illness I should have on the chart?
[SEG0015] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Asthma since he was two. Blue inhaler, ventalin, two puffs when he's wheezy.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. So asthma, ventalin two puffs when wheezy. Oisín, does your head hurt?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is the rash painful when you touch it?
[SEG0019] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Not painful. He scratches it in the evening though.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any trouble with the waterworks?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): My tummy.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Your tummy. Alright. Mam, is the weeing okay? I'll leave the tummy.
[SEG0023] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Weeing is grand. Yeah he just wanted a biscuit.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): With the asthma, any wheeze at night?
[SEG0025] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No... well, sometimes. A whistle after midnight, not every night.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain?
[SEG0027] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Not that either.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Has he had both MMR doses?
[SEG0029] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Umm. The one as a baby, I think. The second, I don't know, doctor, the red book is on the fridge at home.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): You can't mind the second dose, that's fine. Fever since Thursday night is day four, and the rash since yesterday morning is day two.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mouth open for me. Throat is a bit red, and I don't see any Koplik spots inside the cheeks. Ears are clear.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): The rash is blotchy on the tummy, chest and face, and it blanches. Chest is clear, no wheeze just now. Temperature is 38.4, pulse 124, oxygen 98 percent.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Err, I'm not calling it measles for definite. It may be measles given the classmate and the day count, or another viral rash. I can't rule measles out.
[SEG0034] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Do we keep him shut in the house, then?
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Keep him off school, and away from small babies and anyone pregnant, until public health says otherwise. I'll notify them this afternoon.

[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll book a throat swab for measles virus with the nurse before you go. We might do a chest x-ray if that night wheeze doesn't settle. I'll see him on Friday. If the breathing tightens before Friday, come straight back.

spec.situation: Parents of a child with rash and fever after a classmate had measles; vaccination status vague; doctor examines, counts days, plans notification and isolation advice.

traps.happens: The patient denies some symptoms (said as 'no', 'not really', 'never'), has a chronic condition named earlier (for example asthma or hypertension) and later the doctor asks about another symptom of it, and one answer is a double negative or a correction ('not that either', 'no... well, sometimes').
traps.label_rule: Denials go in negative_findings with the exact thing denied, never in symptoms. NEVER write a negative about a condition the patient has said they have. A corrected answer keeps only the final version. A negative is never a symptom, and 'not painful' is the finding 'pain' absent, not a symptom called 'painless'.

features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

bad.reason: Mother says 'Not really' to cough, not a definite absent finding.
Only rash pain on touch is denied; broad 'Pain' is overstated.
Assessment and basis supported, but second MMR was not remembered, not definitely missing.
bad.text: Possible measles or another viral rash (certainty=differential, basis=classmate with measles, day four of fever, day two of rash, second MMR not remembered, stated_by=doctor)

omissions.text: MMR immunisation history was incomplete/uncertain: mother thinks he had the first dose as a baby, but does not know whether he had the second dose.
Chest examination was clear in addition to no wheeze currently.
The doctor explicitly said measles could not be ruled out and was not diagnosing it definitively.
Safety-net advice was to come straight back if breathing tightens before Friday.
